name: 磯鷸
illustrationTaxon: Actitis hypoleucos, monotypic: 19-21 cm. More than for many other waders, behaviour and movements identify Common Sandpiper more than plumage. In flight it has a distinctive staccato style of rapid, shallow wing beats on depressed wings interspersed by short glides. When foraging it habitually bobs its rear end up and down at intervals and adopts a crouched posture. Plumage is rather plain, brown above and on the chest with white underparts and yellowish legs; a short whitish supercilium is more obvious over the lores, and there is a plain pale eye-ring. In flight it shows a white wing bar. Juveniles have more obvious markings above, especially on the wing coverts and tertials.

similarSpecies.distinction: 白腰草鷸背部深褐近黑、佈滿細小白點，腿較長呈暗綠灰，尾上覆羽與尾基白色、飛行時對比強烈；本種背部褐而帶細橫斑、腿短呈黃綠色，尾長伸出翼尖，且不停上下擺動後半身。
林鷸背上有密集的白色斑點、白色眉紋又長又闊且延伸到眼後，腿細長呈黃綠色，多在淡水濕地淺水處涉水；本種背部只有細碎橫斑而無白點，眉紋短、以眼先最明顯，常貼著水邊走並擺尾。

featureNotes: 嘴短、筆直而纖細，基部略淡、末端深色；與白腰草鷸和林鷸相比嘴明顯短一截，是快速判斷的第一個線索（第1圈取自近景圖，實際可見）。
明顯的白色眼圈，配合一段短眉紋——這段眉紋在眼先（嘴與眼之間）最顯眼，是 HKBWS 特別點出的本種特徵（第2圈取自近景圖，實際可見）。
背部與翼上呈暖褐色，覆羽有細碎的深色橫斑；深色翼與褐背之間夾著一塊尖長的白色楔形，是其餘兩種草鷸都沒有的（第3圈取自全身圖，實際可見）。
腿短、呈暗黃綠色，位置偏後；實際野外最實用的其實是行為——覓食時後半身不停上下擺動，並常保持蹲伏姿勢（第4圈取自全身圖，實際可見）。

sources.use: HKBWS substantive read: Category I, a common passage migrant and winter visitor, rare in summer, occurring in a wide variety of freshwater wetlands; 19-21 cm, and more than for many other wader species behaviour and movements identify Common Sandpiper more than plumage, with a distinctive staccato style of rapid shallow wing beats on depressed wings interspersed by short glides in flight and a habit of bobbing its rear end up and down at intervals while adopting a crouched posture when foraging; plumage rather plain, brown above and on the chest with white underparts and yellowish legs, a short whitish supercilium that is more obvious over the lores, and a white wing bar in flight, juveniles having more obvious markings above especially on the wing coverts and tertials; voice a series of two or more high-pitched notes rapidly uttered in a somewhat breathless manner and falling slightly in pitch, with a long alarm whistle that rises slightly and has a clipped ending; occurs in a wide variety of coastal and low-lying wetlands throughout Hong Kong though primarily in the northwest New Territories, with highest numbers in fish pond areas where the bare banks allow foraging at the water's edge; monthly waterbird counts since 1978 show it is most numerous in April in the Deep Bay area but that passage is more prolonged in autumn from August to November, numbers falling midwinter and spring passage evident again in March with fewest birds in June, and the highest count on the Hong Kong side of Deep Bay being 152 on 14 April 2002; systematic counts at the former Kai Tak airport in 1974-79 revealed spring passage by the second week of March with two possible peaks, the first during the second half of March and first week of April and the second and highest during the last week of April and first week of May, passage remaining strong until the third week of May and declining sharply thereafter, autumn passage apparent by the last week of July and peaking during September and October before declining to a low in late January and early February; a count of 20 at San Tin on 6 July 1980 is exceptional as all others primarily involve one or two birds, and the highest single locality winter count away from Deep Bay is 100 at Hebe Haven on 16 February 1985; Sung et al. (2021) concluded the wintering population in Hong Kong declined from 1998 to 2017; forages at the water's edge or on wet or dry mud locating prey visually and sometimes running quickly between short periods of standing still, generally alone and habitually defending feeding territories but coming together to form roosts overnight with pre-roost gatherings such as 55 birds at Mai Po NR on 21 January 2016, and during migration flocks may occur in unusual locations such as at least 50 on Po Toi on 24 April 2006 and 25 on rocks at Cheung Chau on 29 April 1999, with migration at night over Sai Kung recorded; monotypic, breeding across much of the Palearctic between 35N and 70N from western Europe to Kamchatka and wintering in parts of western Europe and north Africa but mainly from sub-Saharan Africa east through the Middle East and the Indian subcontinent to Indochina, south China and southeast Asia down to Australia; in China breeding in the northwest and northeast and wintering in the southern half of the country including Taiwan and Hainan; IUCN Least Concern with a decreasing population trend.

notes: AI 生成插圖，經人眼核對短而直的嘴、白色眼圈與眼先眉紋、翼上細碎橫斑與白色楔形、黃綠色短腿；單型種。
兩隻比較鳥均為 AI 生成示意（白腰草鷸、林鷸，本卡新繪製並已核對），非等比例；卡上不作完整鑑別檢索表。
HKBWS 明言本種「行為比羽色更好認」：覓食時後半身不停上下擺動、常保持蹲伏，飛行時淺而急促的振翅夾著短滑翔——這些動態特徵無法畫進四個圓圈，只寫在卡上的文字說明。
香港最常見的鷸類之一，見於各類海岸與低地濕地，魚塘的裸泥岸數量最多；后海灣最高 152 隻（2002-04-14）。
地圖為 Natural Earth 110m 世界底圖的國家層級概述，不是精確分佈多邊形，繁殖地與越冬地不分工。
IUCN 無危 LC（趨勢下降）；香港屬 Category I，常見過境鳥兼冬候鳥，夏季罕見。
